newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian smoker poisoned by tobacco substitute.
newsitem.headline: Australian smoker poisoned by tobacco substitute.

text.p: An Australian electrician who chewed electrical cable to ease withdrawal pangs from smoking ended up with lead poisoning instead of lung cancer, a medical journal reported.

The man was admitted to hospital last year complaining of abdominal pain and constipation and dcotors found he had blood lead levels three times higher than accepted safety standards, the latest issue of Australian Medical Journal said.

For 10 years the patient chewed almost a metre (yard) a day of the cable, which contains lead to ensure greater flexibility, while working at building sites which prohibited smoking, researchers wrote.
The man told doctors the cable had a "sweet and pleasant taste", especially near the centre.
Regular treatment lowered the man's blood lead levels although he remains a smoker, the journal reported.
